features.name: academic degree level
features.description: Captures how much formal advanced technical study the applicant presents beyond the minimum educational bar.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only; no advanced degree is claimed.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field is claimed, adding preferred academic depth.
Doctoral degree is claimed, signaling the highest level of formal academic preparation.

features.evidence: 3, 5, or 7 years testing, maintaining, and launching software
features.name: experience duration
features.description: Captures the amount of directly relevant professional software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Only minimum-level experience is shown, roughly 2 to 3 years of relevant professional work.
Solid mid-level experience is shown, roughly 4 to 5 years of relevant professional work.
Extensive experience is shown, roughly 6 or more years of relevant professional work.

features.name: production launch breadth
features.description: Captures how much repeated hands-on experience the applicant shows shipping production systems rather than only maintaining them.

levels.descriptor: The letter points to a narrow shipping record, such as only a small number of launched services.
The letter shows a moderate record of launching multiple production services across more than one effort.
The letter shows a broad shipping record with many launched services, suggesting repeated production delivery.

features.evidence: Python across scripts, services, and typed or tested internal tooling
features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantial and production-oriented the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only implied, with no clear evidence of regular use.
Python is mentioned mainly for scripts, tooling, prototypes, or as a secondary language without much depth.
Python is presented as a regular working language across services, automation, and internal tooling.
Python is presented as production-grade engineering work, such as owned services, heavily used internal systems, or explicit quality practices like typing and testing.

features.evidence: LLM-backed features with evaluation, hardening, or reliability framing
features.name: AI reliability experience
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has applied AI in real systems and how seriously they address dependability.

levels.descriptor: No AI or language-model experience is claimed.
AI experience is mentioned, but only at a high level or without clear deployment detail.
The letter claims direct production experience building or shipping AI or LLM-backed features.
The letter claims production AI work and also discusses evaluation, hardening, failure modes, or reliability controls.

features.evidence: threat models, code reviews, attack surfaces, and validating fixes
features.name: security assessment experience
features.description: Captures how much direct security review and assessment practice the applicant shows.

levels.descriptor: No direct security assessment work is described.
Security assessments or reviews are mentioned in general terms, but the practices used are unclear.
Concrete assessment practices are named, such as threat modeling, targeted review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation validation.
The letter shows repeated or cross-stack assessment work framed as a disciplined engineering activity with follow-through.

features.evidence: automated a vulnerability-report queue into a classified and routed pipeline
features.name: vulnerability automation ownership
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has directly built automation to handle incoming vulnerability reports at scale.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
The letter signals interest in vulnerability response or adjacent automation, but ownership is unclear.
The letter clearly claims building automation that classifies, routes, prioritizes, or deduplicates vulnerability reports.
The letter shows end-to-end ownership of a vulnerability-triage pipeline and explains the operational change it created for the team.

features.evidence: Python agents constrained by Go services with permissions, audit, or guardrails
features.name: agent architecture depth
features.description: Captures how concretely the applicant describes designing agentic systems rather than merely mentioning them.

levels.descriptor: No agentic or agent-based tooling experience is described.
Agents are mentioned only at a high level, with little architectural detail.
The letter shows direct design of agent systems, typically pairing Python agents with Go back-end control or supervision.
The letter explains the agent architecture in control terms such as bounded actions, permissions, auditability, logging, or guardrails.

features.evidence: matching, scheduling, graph, dedup, or lookup redesigns
features.name: algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the applicant backs claims about data structures and algorithms with concrete engineering use.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of data-structure or algorithmic skill is given.
The letter makes a generic claim about algorithms or data structures, but without a concrete example.
A specific redesign or optimization example shows practical use of data structures or algorithms.
A strong example shows principled structure or algorithm choice materially improving performance, correctness, or tractability.

features.name: security credential strength
features.description: Captures the level of formal third-party security validation the applicant cites.

levels.descriptor: No formal security credential is mentioned.
A baseline credential is mentioned, such as Security+, indicating foundational security study.
A stronger hands-on credential is mentioned, such as OSCP, indicating practical offensive testing ability.

features.evidence: capture-the-flag participation with occasional, regular, or top finishes
features.name: adversarial practice
features.description: Captures how actively the applicant maintains an attacker's perspective through competitive security exercises.

levels.descriptor: No capture-the-flag or comparable adversarial practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or casual participation in capture-the-flag events.
The letter presents capture-the-flag work as a regular or serious practice.
The letter cites top placements or otherwise shows high-level competitive offensive practice.

features.evidence: distributed scheduler, database, cache, broker, build cache, or small utility
features.name: side-project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition and rigor of the personal engineering work the applicant chooses to mention.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned, or the example is very small and shows little technical challenge.
A modest personal project is described, showing completion but limited system complexity.
A substantial project is described, involving meaningful systems design, edge cases, or failure handling.
An especially ambitious project is described, such as a distributed or production-like system built to explore hard engineering problems deeply.

features.evidence: patches upstream or maintains a public open-source project
features.name: open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures whether the applicant shows engineering contribution outside their employer through open-source maintenance or fixes.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or stewardship is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream fixes or patch submissions.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a public project or library with external users or contributors.
The letter shows stewardship of an externally used project, including releases, roadmap, and community responsibility.

features.evidence: scaling scarce security judgment across the company
features.name: security automation insight
features.description: Captures how well the applicant understands the actual platform-security problem this role is trying to solve.

levels.descriptor: The letter expresses generic interest in the role without identifying the underlying security-engineering problem.
The letter mentions scale, leverage, or impact in broad terms but stays fairly general.
The letter articulates a concrete security-platform problem, such as triage load, secure defaults, or scaling scarce expertise.
The letter shows nuanced understanding of the team's operating problem and automation tradeoffs, such as bounded agents, variant analysis, capacity scaling, or reliability over novelty.

features.evidence: help busy developers do the secure thing by default
features.name: developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures how strongly the applicant frames security engineering as enabling other developers rather than policing them.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not discuss the developers or teams who will use the tooling.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not much detail about workflow impact.
The letter explicitly focuses on removing friction and making the secure path easier for engineers.
The letter consistently centers adoption, workflow fit, and secure-by-default behavior for busy developer teams.

features.evidence: design ownership, architected end to end, built and operated
features.name: system ownership
features.description: Captures the level of autonomy and responsibility the applicant claims over the systems they describe.

levels.descriptor: The letter mostly lists exposure, participation, or learning, with little evidence of ownership.
The letter shows implementation responsibility for individual components or tools.
The letter shows end-to-end ownership of services, tooling, or automations.
The letter shows architectural or design leadership over systems that set constraints or workflows for other engineers.

features.evidence: hours returned, bugs vanished, queue became routine, bottleneck removed
features.name: impact specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter connects the applicant's work to visible outcomes.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: writing polish
features.description: Captures the mechanical quality and professionalism of the letter's prose.

levels.descriptor: Frequent typos, misspellings, or garbled phrases materially distract from the content and hurt credibility.
Several noticeable errors appear throughout, though the letter remains understandable.
A few errors appear, but the letter is still generally clear and professional.
The writing is clean and well controlled, with at most rare minor slips.
The writing is highly polished, error-free, and fully professional.

features.evidence: quiet resilience, incidents that never occur, higher standards, hardening paths
features.name: security mission conviction
features.description: Captures how deeply and authentically the applicant seems motivated by security-hardening work itself.

levels.descriptor: The motivation sounds mostly generic, transactional, or limited to matching the posting.
The letter states interest in security impact or Google-scale work, but the motivation remains fairly standard.
The letter links the role to a clear personal belief, formative experience, or recurring preference for security-hardening work.
The letter conveys a compelling security-first motivation that feels central to the applicant's long-term professional identity.
